key_insight: Truncating positional encodings breaks the usual theoretical equivalence of spectral and walk-based graph features, making some truncated PEs strictly less expressive than expected.
engineering_relevance: For practical GNN design, combining multiple truncated positional encodings can outperform relying on a single family, especially when full O(n^3) encodings are too expensive.
method: Theoretically compare truncated spectral and walk-based positional encodings under graph expressivity tests.
Show that truncated spectral PEs are no longer stronger than 1-WL.
Evaluate a mixed set of truncated PEs and a related family called k-harmonic distances.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports both theoretical results and experiments on real-world datasets showing that a mix of truncated positional encodings is preferable to any single family.
watch_item: Truncated PEs may look similar to their complete versions but can lose expressive power, so implementation choices like how many eigenvectors or adjacency powers to keep matter a lot.
paper_title: Understanding Truncated Positional Encodings for Graph Neural Networks
